profiles.title: The Mother of God: Softener of Evil Hearts
profiles.subject: Theotokos

overview.text: This image is associated with Simeon’s prophecy to Mary in Luke 2:35. The Orthodox Word explains its seven swords as the fullness of her sorrow, especially in witnessing Christ’s suffering and Crucifixion. The date when the type first appeared is unknown.
overview.reason: A necessary concise account of a copyrighted modern publication; no permission to reproduce its full explanation has been established. This is a labelled AI-written summary, not the source author's wording.

blocks.text: The Mother of God is shown without the infant Christ, with three swords on each side and one below. The OCA distinguishes this arrangement from Seven Arrows, whose seven weapons are grouped four on one side and three on the other.

blocks.text: The Orthodox Word separately describes the contemporary travelling image associated with Bachurino. It is a manufactured Sofrino print mounted on wood, not an ancient original. The article relates that it began streaming myrrh after being placed on Saint Matrona’s reliquary in 1999; it later travelled with its guardian Sergei Fomin. The historical reproduction shown here represents the iconographic type and is distinct from that modern travelling print.
